cards.explanation: The answer is Rejoice over him. David says the LORD lifted him up and "…have not allowed my foes to rejoice over me." (Psalm 30:1) Rejoicing over David was the one thing his foes didn't get, friends.
The answer is healed. David says, "O LORD my God, I cried to You for help, and You healed me." (Psalm 30:2) He cried out, and the LORD answered. I like those odds, friends.

The answer is Going down into the Pit. David says, "…You pulled me up from Sheol; You spared me from descending into the Pit." (Psalm 30:3) The Pit was where he was headed, friends, and he didn't go. The LORD spared him.
The word is fleeting, friends. David says, "For His anger is fleeting, but His favor lasts a lifetime." (Psalm 30:5) One passes quickly and the other lasts a lifetime. Easy math.
The answer is Joy, friends. David says, "Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning." (Psalm 30:5) Weeping gets a room for the night. Joy shows up with the morning.

The answer is In prosperity, friends. David says, "In prosperity I said, “I will never be shaken.”" (Psalm 30:6) Things were going well when he said it. I bet most of us have said something like that.

The answer is True, friends. David says, "…You favored me; You made my mountain stand strong. When You hid Your face, I was dismayed." (Psalm 30:7) The mountain was strong, and then he was dismayed. I think that's a lot to take in.

The answer is that if he dies he can't praise the LORD, friends. David asks, "What gain is there in my bloodshed, in my descent to the Pit? Will the dust praise You? Will it proclaim Your faithfulness?" (Psalm 30:9) He wants to be alive to praise the LORD. That's a good reason to ask for help.

The answer is joy, friends. David says, "You turned my mourning into dancing; You peeled off my sackcloth and clothed me with joy…" (Psalm 30:11) The LORD took off the sackcloth and gave him something better to wear. Best outfit change ever.

The answer is so his heart would sing and not be silent, friends! David says the LORD did it "…that my heart may sing Your praises and not be silent." (Psalm 30:12) Look at where the verse ends up. It doesn't stop at the dancing. It lands on praise and on thanks: "O LORD my God, I will give thanks forever." (Psalm 30:12) The sackcloth came off so the singing could start, and David plans to keep it going forever.

The answer is False, friends. David ends with, "O LORD my God, I will give thanks forever." (Psalm 30:12) He doesn't say he'll give thanks only until his troubles are over. He sets no end date, and forever means forever.
